acquisition: Web tool extracted article/abstract bodies. Direct PMC opens sometimes returned CAPTCHA; targeted indexed extraction supplied actual article sections. No full-text access claimed for abstract-only sources.
mechanism: Mirror reflection remains optically continuous. During a gaze shift both eyes rotate; rapid retinal image motion reduces available detail. Perisaccadic stimulus-selective sensitivity loss and masking by adjacent clear fixations reduce awareness of the transient. These mechanisms do not imply total blindness or deleted time. Eye-movement signals also contribute to spatial stability, a related but distinct problem. Later playback decouples the filmed movement from the observer’s current saccade; viewer can hold gaze on screen.
limits: Not a universal impossibility: altered conditions and delayed displays can reveal motion; no clinical claim.
No claim one region shuts off all visual input, or that a mirror itself freezes motion.
No experimentally measured ratio of masking versus extraretinal suppression for this particular demonstration.
